comparator.sourceNotes: Current permitted revisit on 2026-11-13. Exact English-taught full-time BSc Industrial Design, ordinary September 2026 entrant cohort, with no formal specialisations. The current ordinary diagram and after-revision PER PDFs are byte-identical to the prior reviewed sources. All 23 diagram positions total 180 EC (60/60/60): 120 core + 10 ITEC + 50 elective EC, including the 25 EC external learning activity within elective space. The formal PER Article 3.4(3), p22, instead states 125 core EC, Article 3.4(5) separately gives two 5 EC ITEC units, and Appendix 2 p76 requires 50 elective EC (20 in Year 2 and 30 in Year 3), together 185 EC. Article 3.4(8) requires at least 45 elective EC, which does not reconcile Appendix 2. The same PER cohort diagram p78 and current curriculum diagram support 120 core EC, without an explicit correction or precedence for the conflicting text. Appendix 3 MyFuture, sustainability-assessment and calculus pilots do not change these aggregate credits. Current Forms and Files and the PER landing page distinguish after-revision entrants from before-2023 and the separate 2025 cohort diagram. Newly read current Examination Committee Regulations p16 explicitly delegates approval of 50 elective EC for 2023–2024 and later entrants; this corroborates the elective volume but does not amend 125 core EC or reconcile the total. Individual approval/exemption powers are not assumed as a credit waiver. No 5 EC is subtracted or invented. Preserve independent rules: three 5 EC PPD courses, embedded MyFuture pilot and five noncredit SG activities; ELA requires appropriate prior approval and is not a universal internship. BEP entry after 120 earned EC including compulsory Year 1 and DPB240, DCB200, 3PHYS and DLB385 plus signed PlanApp approval; the full assessment table has further course/elective requirements and the partial display is not an entry checklist. Project/PPD progression and all 59 interest judgments, 14 qualified discovery attributions and the actual feasible 24-course internal research remain valid. Publicly retain the 20 named components totalling 130 EC (60/40/30), excluding the conflicted elective space. Full pathway, UCR comparability and final stopping decision remain unapproved pending authoritative reconciliation.

programmes.label: Circular products and sustainable technical systems

alternatives.concept: Study product needs, design and prototyping alongside user behaviour, qualitative inquiry and computational methods for intelligent systems. Programming, data analysis, networks, learning and robot motion support the technical strand;life-cycle assessment, business and ethics support responsible development. This composition is more computational than TU/e's degree and does not reproduce its integrated design-studio, aesthetic or final-project training.
alternatives.labelRationale: Names the completed curricular composition and the explicitly limited academic claim.

alternatives.concept: Combine product and user inquiry with materials science, resource recovery, life-cycle assessment and renewable-energy analysis. Programming, networks, algorithms, mathematics and robot motion support the technical strand, while market research, business and ethics inform responsible development. This option studies sustainability through actual material and energy methods;it does not reproduce TU/e's integrated design studio, aesthetic development or final-project training.
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed programme combines product/customer inquiry, circular-materials and energy methods with a sustained computing/mathematical systems strand. No specialised aesthetic or integrated studio formation is implied.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses/45EC differ in each direction. Materials/wave/chemical foundations, resource-recovery laboratories, renewable-energy systems and climate replace image/predictive/decision/optimisation/reinforcement methods and AI-business analysis. The change gives physical circularity and energy consequences a sustained organising role rather than relabelling the intelligent-product programme.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Actual workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites checked for all six fixed terms. Advisory progression considered; no extra hard prerequisites inferred.

courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Programming Actual Python structured/object-oriented programming, testing and projects; direct programming foundation, not specifically creative interaction design.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Consumer Product Design Actual customer interviews, specifications, product investigation, prototype/production planning, industrial scaling and circularity/economic analysis. Sustained direct physical product design contribution; prototypes where feasible, not promised advanced intelligent hardware.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Product and user inquiry”.

Introduction to Data Science Actual R data cleaning, visualization and research project; direct data-informed design methods, not an interface-design studio.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Mathematical Methods Actual calculus/differential equations and Mathematica dynamic-model project; direct calculus methods.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Research Methods & Statistics Actual surveys/experiments, operationalization, measurement, R and empirical team research; direct user-research methods, not whole design-research process.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Product and user inquiry”.

Social Psychology Actual social cognition/persuasion/group behaviour and literature-based research proposal; direct user/society grounding, not completed usability test.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Product and user inquiry”.

Image Processing & Computer Vision Actual cameras/features/tracking and Python/OpenCV recognition-pipeline project support sensing/intelligent interaction; not embodied sensor electronics.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations Actual customer-needs discovery, design thinking, prototyping, value propositions/business models and startup pitch; direct design/business integration.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Business,ethics and responsible development”.

Linear Algebra Actual matrix/vector/SVD methods and applied computer algebra support robotics and intelligent systems.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Machine Learning Actual statistical/predictive learning, data projects/modelvalidation and limitations support intelligent-system design.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy Actual integrated product/process life-cycle/circularity projects support responsible sustainable product decisions.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Business,ethics and responsible development”.

Qualitative Research Methodology Actual interviewing, observation, participatory/visual methods and team qualitative inquiry support human-centred design research.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Product and user inquiry”.

Marketing & Consumer Engagement Actual consumer research, customer-journey mapping, brand development and strategic recommendations support user/business integration; not a replacement for product-interaction design.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Business,ethics and responsible development”.

Robotics Actual robotarm/gripper programming, kinematics/motion/manipulation and smaller humanrobot/ethics inquiry. Direct physical intelligent-system contribution, not full industrial design project line.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Linear Systems Actual signal/system/control models, Mathematica labs and applied project support sensing/control systems.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Networks & Operating Systems provides network protocols,packet analysis and operating-system resource/concurrency concepts as specific infrastructure for connected intelligent systems; it does not teach interactive electronics. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Decision-making in AI Actual Bayesian/temporal/decision models and multiagent uncertainty support intelligent-system reasoning.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Algorithms & Data Structures Actual algorithms, complexity and experimental benchmarking support computational reliability; complementary foundation.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

Business & Economy in the Age of AI Actual AI business/managerial/economic/societal implications and case projects support responsible innovation strategy; complements rather than duplicates technical ML.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Business,ethics and responsible development”.

Ethics Actual moral argument/theories and independent ethics essays support responsible innovation; no full engineeringethics equivalence.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Business,ethics and responsible development”.

Full contribution to intelligent-system implementation; no physical robot integration guaranteed.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematical and intelligent-system methods”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Include the strongest intelligent-product response,then the materially different circular-product/sustainable-systems response. The earlier feasible circular-business trial was too weak in technical realisation;the stronger second programme adds actual materials,resource-recovery and energy teaching while retaining product/user and computing inquiry. Six different courses/45EC reflect the different organising priorities. A further health-interaction/aesthetic route lacks sustained taught evidence and cannot be supplied by social psychology or art context alone. Stop at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Customer interviews, needs, specifications, concept selection and prototyping address human-centred product development; this does not reproduce the full integrated design studio.
Qualitative design, interviews, observation and analysis supply identifiable empirical inquiry methods; integrated design-research practice is not equated.
StructuredPythonprogramming and computational problem-solving supply direct programming foundations; creative/interactive applications are not guaranteed.
Data preparation, exploration and visualisation are direct parts of data analytics; other statistical training is separate.
Calculus, differential equations and mathematical modelling directly overlap; programme-specific applications differ.
Camera calibration, image representation, filtering and recognition address specific image-based sensing methods. Broader sensor integration and interactive electronics remain gaps.
Design thinking, problem definition, customer discovery, prototyping and value propositions address identifiable innovation methods; sustained design studio remains different.
Life-cycle assessment and circular product/process evaluation directly address sustainability design methods.
Normative ethical theories and applied moral reasoning address the ethical-analysis part; specialised engineering context is not reproduced.

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught TU/e degree combines technology, creativity, user research and business to design interactive products, systems and services. Design projects and a personal development portfolio connect its areas of expertise.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can offer two differently organised academic responses combining real product and user inquiry with intelligent-system methods or circular-materials and sustainable-system methods. UCR does not reproduce TU/e's integrated design-studio, aesthetic, interactive-electronics or final-project training. The unresolved core/elective allocation, including any additional required core study, is outside this comparison. No 45- or 50-EC elective entitlement is assumed.

curriculum.limitation: The nominal degree requires 180 EC. Official sources conflict between 120 and 125 core EC alongside 10 ITEC and 50 elective EC. Only the 130 EC of individually named requirements are shown;the framework has not been reconciled.

componentNotes.DLB384: The personal and professional development learning line comprises three credited 5-EC courses across the degree. MyFuture activities are integrated into this line; at least five Studium Generale activities are also required without additional credits.
componentNotes.DPB390: The final design project requires at least 120 earned credits, the compulsory first-year components and specified second-year courses, together with an approved study plan. Additional course and elective requirements apply; this partial curriculum is not an admission checklist.
